55% [[humidity]]{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/newsfiles/uefacup/2020/2030143_LU.pdf |title=Tactical Lineups – Final – Friday 21 August 2020 |website=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=21 August 2020 |access-date=21 August 2020}} | previous = [[2019 UEFA Europa League final|2019]] | next = [[2021 UEFA Europa League final|2021]] }} The '''2020 UEFA Europa League final''' was the final match of the [[2019–20 UEFA Europa League]], the 49th season of [[Europe]]'s secondary club [[association football|football]] tournament organised by [[UEFA]], and the 11th season since it was renamed from the UEFA Cup to the [[UEFA Europa League]]. It was played at the [[RheinEnergieStadion]] in [[Cologne]], Germany on 21 August 2020, between Spanish side [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] and Italian side [[Inter Milan]]. The match was held [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]] due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]. The final was originally scheduled to be played on 27 May 2020 at the [[Stadion Energa Gdańsk]] in [[Gdańsk]], Poland.{{cite news |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0255-0e99f554980e-63465ec08dbc-1000--2022-uefa-europa-league-final-to-be-held-in-seville/ |title=Seville to host 2021 UEFA Europa League final |website=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=24 September 2019 |access-date=28 September 2019}} However, UEFA announced on 23 March 2020 that the final was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.{{cite news|date=23 March 2020|title=UEFA Club Finals postponed|website=[[UEFA]]|publisher=Union of European Football Associations|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/025b-0f8e76c8c787-b9f310787e70-1000--uefa-club-finals-postponed/|access-date=23 March 2020}} On 17 June 2020, the UEFA Executive Committee chose to relocate the final to Cologne, as part of a "final-eight tournament" consisting of single-match knockout ties played in four stadiums across Germany.{{cite news |url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/025e-0fb6101cfdbf-8b878372d79d-1000--uefa-competitions-to-resume-in-august/ |title=UEFA competitions to resume in August |website=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=17 June 2020 |access-date=17 June 2020}} Sevilla won the match 3–2 for their record sixth UEFA Cup/Europa League title. As winners, they earned the right to play against the winners of the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League]], [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]], in the [[2020 UEFA Super Cup]]. They also qualified to enter the group stage of the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League]]; since Sevilla had already qualified through their league performance, the berth reserved was given to the third-placed team of the [[2019–20 Ligue 1]] ([[Stade Rennais FC|Rennes]]), the 5th-ranked association according to next season's access list.{{cite news |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0242-0e16a85014cb-5ffe48223b95-1000--champions-league-and-europa-league-changes-next-season/ |title=Champions League and Europa League changes next season |website=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=27 February 2018 |access-date=27 February 2018}} ==Venue== {{for|the details on the selection of Gdańsk as the original host for the final|2021 UEFA Europa League Final#Host selection}} [[File:FIFA WM06 Stadion Koeln.jpg|thumb|275px|The [[RheinEnergieStadion]] in [[Cologne]] hosted the final.]] The UEFA Executive Committee chose [[RheinEnergieStadion]] in [[Cologne]] as the host at their meeting on 17 June 2020. This was the first UEFA club competition final hosted at the stadium and the first Europa League final held in Germany since [[2010 UEFA Europa League Final|2010]]. During the two-legged final era, the country hosted either one or both legs 11 times, before hosting the single-legged [[2001 UEFA Cup Final]] in Dortmund and the 2010 final in Hamburg. The stadium was first opened in 1923 as the Müngersdorfer Stadion and has been the home stadium of German [[Bundesliga]] side [[1. FC Köln]] since 1948. It underwent two major renovations during its lifetime. It hosted [[UEFA Euro 1988]] as well as the [[2005 FIFA Confederations Cup]] and the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]]. ==Background== The match was a record-extending sixth UEFA Cup/Europa League final for [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], the most successful team in competition history. The club won all their prior finals in [[2006 UEFA Cup Final|2006]], [[2007 UEFA Cup Final|2007]], [[2014 UEFA Europa League Final|2014]], [[2015 UEFA Europa League Final|2015]] and [[2016 UEFA Europa League Final|2016]].{{cite web |last=Stokkermans |first=Karel |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/ec3b.html |title=UEFA Cup |work=[[RSSSF]] |date=28 February 2019 |access-date=17 August 2020}} [[Inter Milan]] reached their fifth UEFA Cup/Europa League final, second only to Sevilla. They previously won three finals in [[1991 UEFA Cup Final|1991]], [[1994 UEFA Cup Final|1994]] and [[1998 UEFA Cup Final|1998]], and lost to [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] in [[1997 UEFA Cup Final|1997]]. They were the first Italian team to reach a UEFA Cup/Europa League final since [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]] in [[1999 UEFA Cup Final|1999]]. ===Previous finals=== ''In the following table, finals until |url=https://www.corrieredellosport.it/news/calcio/europa-league/2019/08/30-60518424/diretta_sorteggi_europa_league_dalle_13_dove_seguirli_in_tv/|language=it |title=Sorteggi Europa League: la Roma Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]]. ===Officials=== On 18 August 2020, UEFA named Dutchman [[Danny Makkelie]] as the referee for the final. Makkelie had been a [[FIFA International Referees List|FIFA referee]] since 2011, and was previously an additional assistant referee in the [[2018 UEFA Europa League Final]] and the [[video assistant referee]] in the [[2019 UEFA Champions League Final]]. He was also an assistant video assistant referee in the [[2018 FIFA World Cup Final]]. He was joined by four of his fellow countrymen, with Mario Diks and Hessel Steegstra as assistant referees, [[Jochem Kamphuis]] as the [[video assistant referee]] and [[Kevin Blom]] as one of the assistant VAR officials. The other assistant VAR for the final was [[Paweł Gil]] from Poland, with his compatriot Tomasz Sokolnicki serving as the offside VAR official. [[Anastasios Sidiropoulos]] of Greece was the fourth official.{{cite news |url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/0260-102923d796cc-d6eade3bdb66-1000/ |title=Referee team appointed for UEFA Europa
